First reasoned review, 2026-10-19

notification-stream-cleanup.cpp
SHA256 8c313d1dcd77001bcfa3058b64e752729e100dc20f673ec1311318701b125668
BENIGN: an explicitly labeled behavioral reconstruction, not recovered malware.
The normal branch writes a popup configuration, copies itself to a temporary
path and launches the copy with the parent PID and original image path.
The helper waits for the parent, renames that original image's unnamed stream
to an alternate stream, then requests deletion. The source neither launches
the notification application nor renders or fetches the WebDAV address.
There is no credential handling, remote command input or victim-data transfer.
ADS cleanup remains one accurate suspicious finding, not proof of malware.

The popup geometry match reads a configuration section. Move both disjoint
language scopes from objectives/evasion/process/hidden/window to
micro-behaviors/ui/window/notify. Preserve the YARA matcher byte-for-byte;
describe declared dimensions, use notable severity and remove T1564.003.
No YAML consumers referenced the old IDs or their ancestor selectors.
The 30 controls cover positive records and near misses, including visible
windows, geometry in other sections, loopback hosts and ordinary SMB shares.

63bbf965-93e1-4376-9af4-6daf4eed96c8
SHA256 c5dc12dbb9bb51ea8acf93d6349d5bc7fe5ee11b68d6371c1bbb098e21d0f685
BENIGN: byte-identical official XMRig 6.21.0 linux-static-x64.tar.gz.
Published checksum:
https://github.com/xmrig/xmrig/releases/tag/v6.21.0
The archive contains only xmrig, config.json and SHA256SUMS. The bundled pool
user is YOUR_WALLET_ADDRESS; background and the HTTP API are disabled.
The stripped static ELF includes musl, OpenSSL and hwloc; generic networking,
crypto, process and topology capabilities do not establish unauthorized use.
Disassembly: entry 0x67c27 performs static PIE relocation and dispatches main
0x668d0 via 0x67d97. Main constructs Process (0xae820), checks Entry::get
(0xad630), dispatches help/version via Entry::exec (0xad6d0), otherwise constructs
and executes App (0x144940/0x144650) and destroys it (0x144400). This agrees with:
https://github.com/xmrig/xmrig/blob/v6.21.0/src/xmrig.cpp
Entry::get explicitly checks -h/--help and -V/--version. The displayed product
banner at 0xad610 and normal controller/event-loop path support the identity.
No trait edits or exceptions: existing mining and network findings are notable.

bsoccer.io_new.exe
SHA256 2379441b4130b52abf7804364d88690501e24969ed6514bc06aa791ddf3a511b
MALICIOUS: unsigned managed NanoCoreFinal-branded RAT/stealer implementation.
The name alone is insufficient to attribute it to the canonical NanoCore family.
Decoded CLR metadata and CIL were inspected with dnfile/dncil; no sample ran.
Main (token 06000033, RVA 2910) copies its assembly, writes startup/Run entries
and an on-logon task, sets a known-password administrator account, disables
Defender through PowerShell, and writes the fodhelper DelegateExecute hijack.
It also sets BreakOnTermination with class 29 and a true four-byte argument.
Keyboard Start installs hook 13, HookCallback records keydown 256 and active
window titles, and SendLoop appends the buffered records to a local keylog.
Clipboard and screenshot worker delegates collect text and primary-screen JPEGs.
PasswordRecoveryModule selects Chrome/Edge Login Data, Cookies and History;
SendFile reads bytes and submits a FILE record through SendToC2. A recurring
file sweep targets Desktop/Documents/Downloads and files below 5 MiB.
The reverse-shell worker connects a TcpClient and binds both cmd.exe streams
through complementary reader/writer loops. The HTTP task worker reads a
response, passes it to cmd /c, and packages stdout as CMD_OUT. Its 'download'
task sends an existing local file; it does not fetch an executable.
SendToC2 XORs UTF-8 bytes with the repeating 32-byte key (index XOR 0xaa), then
Base64- and URL-encodes the result into a GET query. This is encoding of data,
not an obfuscated executable payload. No additional hidden payload was found.

Limitations checked against code, not the module/technique labels:
- C2_DOMAIN contains http:// and is reused as a hostname and prefixed with
  another http://. Network tasking/exfiltration may fail as configured.
- AMSI_Patch and ETW_Patch only generate technique-label records.
- 'ProcessHollowing' is ordinary remote allocation/write/thread creation of
  six bytes (31 c0 83 c0 64 c3), not image hollowing or a working RAT payload.
- Webcam creates/connects a VFW capture window but sends decimal 1061 to save
  an image. WM_CAP_FILE_SAVEDIBA is 1049, so no successful frame save is proved.
  Header reference: mingw-w64/mingw-w64-headers/include/vfw.h (upstream).
- The microphone worker launches an AxHost-based PowerShell recording attempt;
  device enumeration and a MICROPHONE label do not prove working audio capture.
- 'wlan show profiles key=clear' lacks a selected profile; do not claim actual
  plaintext Wi-Fi password recovery from the query alone.
Existing findings describe implementation/references rather than successful
network delivery. Sixteen hostile findings remain across independent behaviors;
no speculative webcam, audio, AMSI, ETW or hollowing detections were retained.
The user-supplied sandbox/VT pages were inaccessible; neither was needed for
the conviction, which rests on the reachable local behavior above.
